messages:
sara: Heads up — found a repeatable billing drift when clients reconnect mid-stream and our KV cache has evicted prefixes. Repro'd on canary tenant 42.
liam: ugh. can you paste the minimal repro + logs?

sara: repro steps:
1) start streaming generation (client opens ws + stream-id)
2) server emits partial tokens, then toolcall invoked (toolcall_id=tc_77)
3) client disconnects at offset 732
4) client reconnects and resumes using resume_offset=732, but our runtime created a new stream-prefix chunk rather than reusing KV snapshot because the old cache was evicted
5) the toolcall token batch gets re-emitted on resume path and billing counts it as a fresh toolcall -> duplicate charge

liam: logs:
```
INFO stream=2034567890 resume_offset=732 evt=resume start_ts=2034567890
INFO toolcall tc_id=tc_77 billed=true billing_ctx=stream_chunk_2
WARN kv_cache evict key=stream_2034567890_chunk_1
INFO toolcall tc_id=tc_77 billed=true billing_ctx=stream_chunk_3
```

anita: so we charged tc_77 twice because billing attributes by chunk id instead of global toolcall id. nice catch.

jason: how often does this happen? is it only when eviction compacts keys or every reconnect?

sara: depends on memory pressure. on canary it was ~1.2% of reconnects. on prod it's rare but shows up as small monthly drift for some orgs.

liam: proposed fixes:
- server assigns a durable `toolcall_id` (UUID) at first emission and persists it to the stream state store; on resume we dedupe billing by that id (low complexity, needs small state write per toolcall)
- or emit provisional credits on resume then reconcile on finalization (complex UI + bookkeeping)
- or expand KV retention to avoid eviction (expensive)

anita: prefer the `toolcall_id` path. It's deterministic, keeps billing logic simple (single canonical id), and avoids UX churn.

jason: +1. question: where do we persist the id? local ephemeral vs central state? if central, write amplification under high-throughput streams.

liam: we can piggyback on existing stream metadata writes (we already checkpoint offsets). add a short-lived `toolcall_id` map alongside offsets. Writes are already batched, so marginal cost should be small.

sara: telemetry needs:
- metric: `stream.toolcall.duplicate_charge_total` (tag by org, model, node)
- metric: `stream.resume_with_eviction_total`
- trace span annotation: `toolcall.id` and `billing_status:{provisional|final|deduped}`
- a console toggle to show "provisional charges" in trace view for rollout

anita: also add a reconciliation gauge: `stream.toolcall.reconciled_delta` so finance can monitor reconciles.

jason: rollout plan idea:
- implement server-generated `toolcall_id` + dedupe logic in billing pipeline
- add telemetry and a debug-only trace flag
- deploy to 5% of runtime nodes, enable billing dedupe for a tiny canary org, run for 72h
- if good, expand to 25%, then full

liam: PR checklist:
- [ ] runtime: generate/persist `toolcall_id` (small schema bump)
- [ ] billing: dedupe by `toolcall_id` if present, fall back to existing heuristics
- [ ] telemetry: metrics + tracing annotations
- [ ] console: add provisional charge indicator in per-request traces
- [ ] e2e test: simulate reconnect + eviction

sara: I'll own runtime change. anita can own billing dedupe. jason will own telemetry + console bits.

anita: one open question — what about legacy streams without persisted id? billing fallbacks should remain as-is and mark those reconciles with `legacy=true` tag.

liam: agree. also add a `billing.reconcile.hold_window` config (default 10s) so we avoid races when final ack arrives right after resume.

deploy-bot: starting canary deploy: runtime v0.52.3 -> 5% nodes (tag: stream-toolcall-dedupe)

billing-bot: provisional credits will be emitted with tag `provisional=true` for canary org id 42

sara: after canary we'll run a quick accounting job to compare per-org monthly deltas for affected orgs and sanity-check with finance.

jason: I'll add the console flag behind `platform.featureFlags.showProvisionalCharges` and wire the trace UI to display `billing_status`.

anita: scheduling PR reviews. ETA merge -> canary deploy tomorrow AM.

liam: thanks all. great cross-team response. if we see anything odd, escalate to incidents.

sara: +1 :thumbsup:\n
